items.title: A Medieval Christmas Tradition - A Victorian Recipe!
items.description: A baked boar's head was a medieval tradition at Christmas. This tradition continued for centuries, and on Queen Victoria's Christmas sideboard in 1888 at Osborne House, we can see a decorated boar's head on display. Charles Elmé Francatelli was a famous Victorian chef and in one of his cook books is a complicated recipe for 'Imitation Boar's Head'. Was this the dish served to Queen Victoria in 1888? global_silver_linings.title: Africa’s Wildfire Season Is Actually Getting Shorter, Scientists Think They Know Why
global_silver_linings.snippet: A changing climate seems to be shortening Africa’s dry season, resulting in less land scorched during the wildfire season according to new science. For all the column inches devoted to the record wildfire seasons in France, Spain, or the Amazon, it is still and has always been Africa that’s the center of world wildfires. 70% […] The post Africa’s Wildfire Season Is Actually Getting Shorter, Scientists Think They Know Why appeared first on Good News Network .
global_silver_linings.reason: Africa's wildfire seasons are shrinking, and scientists are closing in on the reasons why — a genuine sign that ecosystems and human behaviour can shift in the right direction. Understanding the cause puts us in a much stronger position to protect the continent's extraordinary landscapes and wildlife.

global_silver_linings.reason: Maasai warriors, once celebrated for proving their courage by hunting lions, are now channelling that same bravery into protecting them — a remarkable cultural shift that is helping lion populations recover across Kenya. It's a reminder that the people closest to nature are often its most powerful defenders.

discovery_articles.title: Roman Theatre of Catania in Catania, Italy
discovery_articles.snippet: Via Vittorio Emanuele II is one of Catania's main thoroughfares, running east to west through the city center and several notable piazzas. Near the road's midpoint, through the front doors of a nondescript two storey building is the Teatro Romano di Catania, a Roman theater dating from the 1st century AE. The theatre was constructed over an old Greek theatre, that was likely the setting for Alcibiades’ speech to Catanaeans in 415 BC, persuading them to ally with Athens against Sparta and Syracuse during the Peloponnesian Wars.

featured_read.title: Kahlil Gibran on Silence, Solitude, and the Courage to Know Yourself
featured_read.snippet: "In much of your talking, thinking is half murdered. For thought is a bird of space, that in a cage of words may indeed unfold its wings but cannot fly."
featured_read.blurb: Gibran's quietly radical argument is that most of our talking is a way of hiding from ourselves — and that the real act of courage is learning to sit with the unspoken. Save this for a morning when the house is still.
